nodes.label: Users Exist Now, Authentication Does Not
nodes.rationale: Creating users alongside the tables that reference it satisfies the ordering constraint at the schema level for the price of one migration instead of five. password_hash is a column with a home, not a claim that anything safe fills it yet.

nodes.label: Roles Are a Column, Not Three Tables
nodes.rationale: A roles table plus permissions plus a join table would be three joins to resolve three constant values — machinery with no question to answer. It becomes a table the moment a role is something a user can define.

nodes.label: Events Are Truth; State Is a Projection
nodes.rationale: fills is append-only and authoritative; positions and equity_points are stored only because recomputing a portfolio from every fill on each page load would be absurd. rebuild_from_fills regenerates positions and a test asserts the result matches, so the claim is checked rather than asserted. The same reasoning gives bars a revision rather than an in-place edit.

nodes.label: Three Primary Key Strategies
nodes.rationale: UUIDv7 for entities so an object knows its id before commit and inserts land at the right-hand edge of the index; BIGINT identity plus UNIQUE(event_id) for trades and quotes because eight bytes against sixteen repeats across every index on the largest tables; natural composites for bars and positions because their identity is the composite and it is exactly the index the read path wants.

nodes.label: Idempotency Lives in the Schema
nodes.rationale: Kafka delivers at least once, so every ingestion path will be called twice. UNIQUE(event_id), the revision-guarded bar upsert, UNIQUE(client_order_id) and UNIQUE(alert_rule_id, dedupe_key) absorb that in the database, where it holds across a restart and a second replica in a way in-process state could not.

nodes.label: Native Enums With Values Spelled Out
nodes.rationale: SQLAlchemy persists enum member names by default, so BarInterval.ONE_MINUTE would be stored as ONE_MINUTE while configuration, logs and the wire format all say 1m; values_callable fixes it and a migration test asserts the labels. Types are dropped explicitly because PostgreSQL leaves them behind and the next upgrade fails on 'type already exists'.

nodes.label: Case-Insensitive Email Without citext
nodes.rationale: A unique index on lower(email) gives the same guarantee with no extension dependency, since managed PostgreSQL does not always allow extensions, and the stored value keeps the case the user typed. The cost is that every lookup must say lower(email) = lower(:email) — which the repository does, in one place.

nodes.label: What Is Deliberately Not Constrained
nodes.rationale: A constraint that rejects real data is worse than no constraint. Quotes may be crossed because locked and crossed markets are real and precisely the moments worth keeping; positions and cash may go negative so a bug in the execution simulator is exposed rather than hidden; ingested_at may precede occurred_at because provider clocks drift and dropping real data over someone else's NTP is the worse failure.

nodes.label: Cascade Policy
nodes.rationale: Everything a user owns cascades on delete because there is no real money and no retention requirement, so 'delete my account' should actually delete it. Two exceptions: instruments use ON DELETE RESTRICT because a delisted symbol changes status rather than taking its price history with it, and audit_log.user_id is SET NULL because the record that an action happened outlives the account that performed it.

nodes.label: Indexes, Each for a Named Query
nodes.rationale: Every index exists for a named query and a test checks both that it exists and that the query uses it. There is deliberately no index on trades.occurred_at alone: no current query needs it and an unused index still costs a write on every insert into the largest table. Column order matters because a B-tree can only seek on the leading column.

nodes.label: NUMERIC Money and TIMESTAMPTZ Time
nodes.rationale: A test asserts 0.1 + 0.2 == 0.3 through a round trip, which is false in binary floating point and true here. A schema test asserts no timestamp column is TIMESTAMP WITHOUT TIME ZONE, because that is the bug that shows up twice a year.

nodes.label: Growth Escalation Path for trades/quotes
nodes.rationale: Indexing, then native range partitioning by month, then retention and downsampling, then TimescaleDB. Each step is taken when a measurement shows the previous one is insufficient. No step has been taken, because no measurement exists yet.
